scope: Original canonical fixtures with separately named presentation styles. The Lua renderer preserves each validated instance and document view.

profiles.title: Asymmetric garden
profiles.note: An original asymmetric panel guided by the adaptive botanical method. The empty center is reserved by the layout.

profiles.title: Masked periodic repeat
profiles.note: A repeat in a fixed document frame. The compact fixture demonstrates that a protected region removes paint without reindexing tiles.

profiles.title: Celtic strand
profiles.note: A planar strand with validated over and under crossings. The color treatment retains the strand graph and crossing assignment.

profiles.title: Polygons in contact
profiles.note: The linework comes from admitted polygon contacts. Unsupported ray configurations are reported, and the protected opening is explicit.

profiles.title: Freeform star ornament
profiles.note: A finite arrangement of mixed star orders on a validated scaffold. The gallery view does not expand the supported circle-packing domain.

profiles.title: Chair substitution
profiles.note: A compact finite chair patch with explicit substitution lineage. Enlarging the presentation does not add cells.

profiles.title: Penrose P3
profiles.note: Thin and thick rhombs come from the regular pentagrid. The fixed frame and global cell identities remain the same in both views.

profiles.title: Spectre patch
profiles.note: A finite Spectre construction with matching curved seams. The source scope is distinct from the Hat and Tile(1,1).

profiles.title: Ammann–Beenker squares and rhombs
profiles.note: A tetragrid window generates square and rhomb cells with stable world identities and explicit phase.

profiles.title: Bounded square completion
profiles.note: An explicitly bounded solve with marked edges and a constrained route. The fixture makes no unbounded tiling claim.

profiles.title: Gothic tracery
profiles.note: A two-dimensional arch and foil construction using admitted parameters. This is separate from the spatial curve-network example.

profiles.title: Periodic Escherization
profiles.note: A verified periodic witness reused without an optimizer. It represents one admitted result; other Escherization profiles have separate evidence.

profiles.title: Partial mosaic
profiles.note: Original field-guided tile placement with explicit partial-packing status. The open grout remains visible.

profiles.title: Field-guided hatching
profiles.note: Hatching follows an analytic field. Stippling and example-driven synthesis are checked separately in the same family.

profiles.title: Tone-guided maze
profiles.note: An analytic tone field controls spacing and weight. The finite maze and its solution keep their graph semantics through render changes.

profiles.title: Micrography
profiles.note: Original text and the pinned Latin Modern derivative form the rendered lines. Visible outlines accompany an ordered logical text layer.

profiles.title: DecoBrush exemplar synthesis
profiles.note: An original exemplar library guides the brush shape and its attached feature. The clean view preserves the open loop in the finite silhouette.

profiles.title: Projected spatial ogees
profiles.note: A projection of the validated 3D curve network. Download the network alongside the view to retain its spatial geometry.

profiles.title: Inline garden divider
profiles.note: An original collection member with explicit physical placement and a preserved ornament instance.

profiles.title: Hat clusters
profiles.note: An admitted finite Hat cluster with its prototype labels and outline. Its hierarchy is kept separate from Spectre.

profiles.title: Authored floral margin
profiles.note: The original authored layout is captured as a validated legacy scene. The revised paint is a separate gallery recipe.

profiles.title: Grown floral margin
profiles.note: The legacy procedural growth instance keeps its seed and original spatial arrangement. The gallery revision changes paint only.
